description:
handle_call(:compact, ...) (server.ex:213-223) is the only entry to Logic.start_compaction/1, and NOTHING in lib/ or test/ ever sends it. So the compaction cutover — and with it the snapshot upload at handle_info({:compaction_ready, ...}) — never runs in production. The only snapshot a materializer actually writes is upload_snapshot_before_spindown/1 at idle spin-down.

That makes 'snapshot on a schedule' impossible today, which is the half of bedrock-zi44 that shipped as a throttle (snapshot_min_interval_ms) rather than a scheduler. bedrock-zi44 deliberately did NOT solve it by putting the cutover on a timer: a scheduled cutover multiplies two pre-existing defects by the configured cadence (see the atomic double-apply bug and the locked-worker puller bug filed alongside), and it produces nothing for an idle shard anyway — the snapshot key is the durable version and Snapshot.write is put-if-not-exists, so an idle shard re-PUTs the identical bundle to the identical key. Probed: eleven uploads in 500ms, one object.

What is actually needed is either (a) a compaction policy — something that decides when a shard should compact, at which point bedrock-zi44's policy already gates the resulting upload — or (b) a way to produce the bundle without a full cutover, the way upload_snapshot_before_spindown/1 does with scratch files, run off the GenServer so it does not stall the applier.

Whichever it is, bedrock-zi44's SnapshotPolicy is the seam: decide/2 already answers 'is this opportunity worth an upload'.
title: Nothing drives Olivine compaction: a running materializer never snapshots
